title: INR Trend on Warfarin Therapy
scenario: A 66-year-old female client with atrial fibrillation is taking warfarin for stroke prevention. The nurse reviews serial INR results after a recent dose increase.

tabs.title: Anticoagulation Flowsheet
rows: Reports gum bleeding when brushing teeth
Bruising on arms; blood in urine

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: Reviewing the four-week INR trend, what is the nurse's priority concern at Week 4?

options.text: The INR has risen well above the therapeutic range and the client shows signs of bleeding
The warfarin dose is subtherapeutic and needs to be increased
The INR is within the target range and no action is needed
The client is at risk for clot formation from under-anticoagulation

questions.rationale: The INR climbing from 2.4 to 3.8 to 5.2 with gum bleeding, bruising, and hematuria indicates over-anticoagulation and active bleeding risk, which is the priority concern requiring intervention.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: Based on the Week 4 trend, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hold the warfarin dose and notify the provider
Assess for further signs of bleeding
Anticipate an order for vitamin K
Administer an additional dose of warfarin
Give protamine sulfate to reverse the warfarin

questions.rationale: A supratherapeutic INR with active bleeding calls for holding warfarin, provider notification, anticipating vitamin K (the warfarin antidote), and bleeding precautions. Giving more warfarin worsens the risk, and protamine reverses heparin, not warfarin.
